children: GSK said it agreed to buy an early-stage antibody-based treatment from biotechnology company Chimagen Biosciences in a deal valued at up to $750 million.
The London-listed pharmaceutical company said Tuesday that it would acquire Chimagen's trispecific T-cell engager (TCE) treatment and plans to develop it to treat the blood cancer multiple myeloma.
Multiple myeloma is generally considered treatable but isn't currently curable. Other TCE drugs have helped transform treatment but have difficult tolerability profiles, GSK said.

Chimagen's TCE is designed to improve tolerability and efficacy by binding to T-cells while also targeting two tumor-associated antigens, the company said. GSK hopes this will help drive wider adoption and earlier use in multiple myeloma treatment.
GSK will pay an upfront fee to acquire full global rights to the TCE program, and plans to advance the TCE into Phase 1 trials in 2027.
Chimagen will also receive success-based development and commercial milestone payments, GSK said.
